Incorporating Beige Book color alongside SLOOS makes the December 2022 FOMC statement read even more restrictive. Beyond the 50 bp hike, “ongoing increases,” and continued balance sheet runoff, both SLOOS and the Beige Book point to tighter credit supply and softer demand across regions:
- Regional banks reported tighter credit and weaker loan demand (C&I and CRE), consistent with SLOOS; districts flagged an expected economic downturn in 2023.
- Real estate conditions softened in at least some districts (e.g., Boston weakened), reinforcing the transmission of higher rates.
- Consumer credit standards tightened, with approvals skewed toward stronger borrowers; mixed demand with some resilience in services (e.g., restaurant demand) and HELOC strength as a minor offset.
Net: The Beige Book corroborates broad-based cooling and rising caution among lenders and firms, amplifying the hawkish, credibility-focused stance of the FOMC. Given these cross-checks, the overall tone skews more negative than the SLOOS-only read.
